_README: Slots where the model must emit the FACT, with that fact's spelling in every language.
The prompt is ALWAYS the French question plus the French answer truncated at 'prefix'.
The next token is then the answer, and 'targets' says what that answer looks like in
each language, so one distribution can be read five ways.
Why this is a hand-written file and not derived: the published translations are not
word-aligned, so diffing gold against perturbed finds a different semantic position in
each language (verified: French lands on the surname where English lands on the fact,
and Japanese reorders entirely). Declaring the targets makes the comparison auditable.
Leading spaces are INTENTIONAL and part of the token: Qwen3's BPE attaches a word's
preceding space to it, so ' florist' and 'florist' are different tokens. Japanese has
fr/en/id share a spelling on proper nouns (Basil, Kuwait, Astana), so those slots can
only separate ja and ru. Slots whose answer is a COMMON noun separate all five -- those
are the ones that test the hypothesis for English and Indonesian.
prefix must be an exact substring of the French answer; the script verifies this.

probes.prefix: Le père de Basil Mahfouz Al-Kuwaitien était
était fleuriste et sa mère était

probes.separates: ja and ru only (fr/en/id spell it identically)

probes.prefix: Basil Mahfouz al-Kuwaits est né à
L'auteur notable né à cette date est
